imageryNote: Satellite crops are Copernicus Sentinel-2 L2A, 10 m multispectral pixels, rendered from the Microsoft Planetary Computer mirror of the Copernicus archive. Each frame is labeled with the scene acquisition time in the product metadata. Cloud cover is the scene-level figure, not a measurement inside the crop. Downloading pixels from the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem itself needs CDSE credentials; the scheduled job searches CDSE and falls back to Planetary Computer for the image. Frames are not a construction survey.

sites.name: Vineland, New Jersey
sites.relationship: Build with DataOne. The November 12, 2025 prospectus supplement says the Microsoft agreement is for dedicated capacity at the new data center in Vineland, New Jersey.
sites.status: Partial delivery. More than half of the Microsoft-contracted capacity is expected by year-end 2026, and the rest in the second quarter of 2027.
sites.capacity: Expandable up to 300 MW (March 5, 2025). 200 MW contracted and in construction as of August 7, 2025. Microsoft contract value about $17.4 billion through 2031, or about $19.4 billion if Microsoft takes the additional services. Megawatts energized were not stated.
sites.dates: Prospectus supplement November 12, 2025: obligations commenced in early November 2025, tranches during 2025 and 2026. November 12, 2026 letter: remaining tranches moved, in part because temporary generation was retired ahead of Bloom fuel cells.

pin.precision: City centroid of Vineland, New Jersey, the municipality named in the November 12, 2025 prospectus supplement. Not a facility coordinate.

sites.notes: The August 7, 2025 shareholder letter spelled the location Vinefield. The later prospectus says Vineland. This page uses Vineland and does not treat the two spellings as two sites.

contractedOrPlanned.label: Contracted, as of August 7, 2025
contractedOrPlanned.note: 200 MW contracted and in construction on that date, expandable up to 300 MW in the March 5, 2025 post. The November 12, 2026 letter does not restate a megawatt total. It says more than half of the Microsoft-contracted capacity is expected by year-end 2026 and the rest in the second quarter of 2027. The half was not given in megawatts.

operational.label: Partial, megawatts not stated
